source: so there will be a lobby and U go up to someone and ask if I want to dance battle and then they decline or accept if they accept U teleport to an arena and choose a phonk song and dance battle first one to 3 gets 50+ arua and wins and say U only win one round U only get 20+ arua but if U win 2 rounds you get 30+ arua and with that arua U can buy a new emote and depend on the rarity of ur emote U have better chances of winning and each emote has an ability

image_prompt.text: Markers that move a challenger and the player who accepted out of the lobby and into the battle arena, and back when it ends
An out-of-play area for players who are not in the current battle to stand and watch
A prominent wall in the lobby sized to host the game's global leaderboard
an open lobby where players walk up to each other to ask for a dance battle
a dance battle arena - a flat performance floor with room for two dancers facing off

layout_placement.text: Lobby-to-arena transport fired when a challenge is accepted
Detection that registers a won round, first to 3 rounds taking the battle
Leaderboard surface driven by aura totals
two facing start marks on the arena floor, one per dancer

notes: The challenge handshake - walk up, ask, accept or decline - is behaviour, but it needs the lobby to put players within talking distance.
Phonk song selection, the aura currency, the emote shop, emote rarity and per-emote abilities are progression and interface systems with no layout footprint.
Rarity improving a player's chance of winning is a scoring rule, not a spatial one.

open_questions.ask: No look was described - should the lobby and arena read as a neon club, a street corner, or something else?
How many players should the lobby hold, and should more than one battle run at a time?
Is there one shared arena, or a separate arena instanced per battle?

coverage_missing.ask: What should the lobby and arena look like?
How many players in the lobby, and one arena or many?
Can spectators watch a battle, or is the arena private to the two dancers?

answers.ask: No look was described - should the lobby and arena read as a neon club, a street corner, or something else?
answers.answer: Make it a neon club theme, which fits the phonk music and dance battles.

answers.ask: How many players should the lobby hold, and should more than one battle run at a time?
answers.answer: Keep the lobby small at about 10 players, and allow more than one battle to run at a time.

answers.ask: Is there one shared arena, or a separate arena instanced per battle?
answers.answer: Use separate instanced arenas per battle so each accepted dance battle has its own match.
